name: FOREIGN KEY.sql - Copy.txt
content:
-- Start fresh
DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS SchoolDB;
CREATE DATABASE SchoolDB;
USE SchoolDB;
-- +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
-- (Just to confirm it's empty)
SHOW TABLES;   -- Expected: Empty result
-- +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++

-- Create parent table
CREATE TABLE Departments (
    DeptID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    DeptName VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL
);

-- Create child table (NO cascade yet → default is RESTRICT)
CREATE TABLE Students (
    StudentID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    StudentName VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    DeptID INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (DeptID) REFERENCES Departments(DeptID)
);
-- +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
-- Seed data
INSERT INTO Departments VALUES (1, 'Computer Science'),(2, 'Mechanical'),(3, 'Civil');
INSERT INTO Students VALUES (101, 'Alice', 1), (102, 'Bob', 1), (103, 'Charlie', 2), (104, 'David', 3);
-- +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
-- Try deleting DeptID=1 (REFERENCED by Alice & Bob)
-- EXPECTED: This will FAIL with a foreign key constraint error (RESTRICT)
DELETE FROM Departments WHERE DeptID = 1;

-- Check current data (nothing changed because delete failed)
SELECT * FROM Students;
SELECT * FROM Departments;
-- +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++

-- Recreate Students with ON DELETE SET NULL and ON UPDATE CASCADE
DROP TABLE Students;

CREATE TABLE Students (
    StudentID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    StudentName VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    DeptID INT,
    CONSTRAINT fk_dept
        FOREIGN KEY (DeptID) 
        REFERENCES Departments(DeptID)
        ON DELETE SET NULL
        ON UPDATE CASCADE
);

-- Re-insert the same student data
INSERT INTO Students VALUES
(101, 'Alice', 1),
(102, 'Bob', 1),
(103, 'Charlie', 2),
(104, 'David', 3);
-- +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++

-- Now DELETE a parent row where children exist → DeptID=2
-- EXPECTED: Succeeds; Charlie’s DeptID becomes NULL (because ON DELETE SET NULL)
DELETE FROM Departments WHERE DeptID = 2;

-- Verify the delete effect
SELECT * FROM Departments;  -- DeptID 2 is gone; 1 and 3 remain
SELECT * FROM Students;     -- Charlie's DeptID is now NULL
-- $$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$
-- *** Test ON UPDATE CASCADE ***

-- Change DeptID=3 to DeptID=30 in Departments
UPDATE Departments SET DeptID = 30 WHERE DeptID = 3;

-- EXPECTED: David’s DeptID auto-updates from 3 → 30 (cascade)
SELECT * FROM Departments;  -- Should show DeptID 1 and 30
SELECT * FROM Students;     -- David now has DeptID = 30
